sources.use: Arenicola-Nipponocirsium split 1.02 Mya; C. brevicaule-C. irumtiense split ~0.93 Mya; C. morii split ~0.79 Mya; East Asian topology and tip colours.
Within Taiwanese Nipponocirsium sensitivity scaffold: C. pengii basal, ~0.47 Mya; C. kawakamii-C. tatakaense split ~0.35 Mya; alternative basal resolutions retained as sensitivity.

analysis_question: Does adding published time information make the Arenicola flower-colour ancestor identifiable, or is the coloured-ancestor preference still conditional on a low transition-rate assumption?
claim_boundary: This is a hybrid published-node-age sensitivity scaffold, not an extracted BEAST/ASTRAL Newick tree and not the Moreyra final tree. Node ages come from two related East Asian studies with different sampling/analyses. It is used only to diagnose rate/topology identifiability. No final stochastic map, posterior ancestral probability, diversification-rate inference, or published-tree likelihood claim is permitted.
